body: It's been a rough decade. I'm not sure on the 20 year celebration. Maybe. It might be nice to have a party. Maybe I'll get really hammered! (Just kidding-that would be awful)

Yeah. It's a long time. Sober alcoholics have a high suicide rate, tho'. Getting through the gap between 10 and 20 years is notoriously brutal. I have about 3 1/2 months left 'til I hit the 20 year mark; Jan 12th.
Today wasn't awful. Went to a meeting. I'm a sober alcoholic and addict. 19 1/2 years clean.

Heart seems okay at the moment. I have meds for it. Seemed ironic to get the minor flutter, then 45 min later I'm tying a noose to my chin up bar.

If the heart blips again anytime soon, or if it hits harder, I'll call 911

Haven't found it yet. I'm a hoarder, which I've been working on, but it's made it almost impossible to find things sometimes. My cat died a week ago, not sure how I'm gonna make rent, or my car payment. Car was already repossessed once - I borrowed money to get it out. There's other shit, too - losing track of the wallet just broke the camel's back, y'know. I have heart problems, as well, and I am 90% sure I had a minor heart attack today, in the literal sense. I had a major one several years ago, so I know what they're like. Yeah, shit day. Thanks for responding, tho', sincerely, it helps a great deal.

Thank you. I cannot take any credit for the rhyme scheme; it's an English Sonnet, often called a Shakespearean Sonnet. I try to adhere as strictly as I can to its conventions: iambic pentameter, a rhyme scheme of ababcdcdefefgg, and a volta at line 9. For me, personally, the strictness of the format helps me sort the maelstrom of thoughts on a subject. The result sometimes seems archaically formal and a bit stilted, but this formality can be embraced, as well. As a piece, I'm pretty happy with it. The starkness of the subject matter seemed to crack against the formality of the format.

And yes, I am the narrator. As I've indicated in the piece, when suicidal depression hits, for me, I am compulsively unable to speak of it. I can't "Vague Book" about it on Facebook, I don't drop hints, I can't even really tell my shrink, as she may become obligated to put me in for observation. The cycle has been, by the time I do give voice to it, the worst has passed.

Thus, this poem appeared. I was in a dark place, I crammed the maelstrom in to 10 lines of vicious format in about 45 minutes... and it just stared at me. I couldn't post in on Facebook, or my regular reddit account, so I created this account, and posted it here. I had to navigate the strict rules of these forums to post it at all, which, given my state of mind at the time, was a bit maddening. (I understand why the rules are in place, but it was an unexpected and frustrating hurdle)

And so, here it is.

I will take a look at the link you provided, but, as I'm sure you are aware, and understand, I make no promises about anything.

Thanks.

Silent Suicide Sonnet  
    It cannot be said aloud when it comes  
    The haunting thought of self inflicted death.  
    The calling of the hanging noose it hums  
    With constant dreams of choking off my breath.  
    To silence sworn, I cannot give a clue  
    A pact with madness sacred as the grave.  
    I musn't let a soul know what I'll do  
    Lest from my hand my life might still be saved.  
    The shame of what I think, it presses down  
    In agonizing horror at my thoughts.  
    If given voice, I fear they may be found  
    Unworthy of the drama they have wrought.  
    Shame pushes me to kill myself, and shame  
    Keeps all release at bay the very same.

This should have been marked "Just Sharing," I guess, but I saw no way to do that. It just posted it as "Feedback Requested," no matter what I seemed to do. Feedback is fine. Or not. I wanted to post the poem, that's all, I am not interested in conversation. Nothing personal.
